title: Module Review Quiz: Smart Pointers & Resource Management

slides.title: Smart Pointers & Resource Management Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers memory leaks, std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, std::weak_ptr, make_unique, make_shared, custom deleters, and circular reference resolution in C++ (CPP_257 to CPP_264).

slides.title: Memory Header Inclusion (CPP_257)
slides.prompt: Fill in the header file name required to use C++ Smart Pointers.

slides.title: std::unique_ptr Ownership (CPP_258)
slides.prompt: Which statement best describes the ownership model of std::unique_ptr?
options: Exclusive single ownership; cannot be copied, only moved
Shared ownership; can be copied freely across threads
Non-owning weak reference to heap memory
Automatic conversion to raw pointers on assignment
slides.correctAnswer: Exclusive single ownership; cannot be copied, only moved

slides.title: std::make_unique Factory (CPP_258)
slides.prompt: Fill in the helper function name introduced in C++14 to safely allocate a unique_ptr.

slides.title: Moving std::unique_ptr (CPP_258)
slides.prompt: How do you transfer ownership of a std::unique_ptr 'p1' to 'p2'?

slides.title: std::shared_ptr Declaration (CPP_259)
slides.prompt: Fill in the smart pointer type used when multiple owners need to share a resource.

slides.title: std::shared_ptr Reference Counting (CPP_259)
slides.prompt: When is the dynamic heap memory owned by a std::shared_ptr actually deallocated?
options: When the internal reference count drops to zero
Immediately when the first shared_ptr goes out of scope
When std::move() is called on any instance
At the end of the main() function strictly
slides.correctAnswer: When the internal reference count drops to zero

slides.title: Reference Count Query (CPP_260)
slides.prompt: Fill in the member function name used to check the current reference count of a shared_ptr.

slides.title: Circular Reference Issue (CPP_261)
slides.prompt: What major memory bug occurs when two std::shared_ptr objects hold shared references to each other?
options: A circular reference memory leak (objects are never destroyed)
slides.correctAnswer: A circular reference memory leak (objects are never destroyed)

slides.title: std::weak_ptr Declaration (CPP_261)
slides.prompt: Fill in the non-owning smart pointer type used to break circular shared_ptr references.

slides.title: Accessing std::weak_ptr (CPP_261)
slides.prompt: Which method must be called on a std::weak_ptr to safely acquire a std::shared_ptr before reading data?

slides.title: Raw Pointer Access (CPP_262)
slides.prompt: Fill in the member function used to extract the underlying raw pointer from a smart pointer.

slides.title: Custom Deleter (CPP_263)
slides.prompt: Why might you pass a Custom Deleter to a std::unique_ptr or std::shared_ptr?
options: To manage non-heap resources like custom C-style file handles or API cleanup functions
To speed up memory allocation on low-RAM devices
To bypass access specifiers in C++ classes
To convert smart pointers into static global variables
slides.correctAnswer: To manage non-heap resources like custom C-style file handles or API cleanup functions

slides.title: Resetting Smart Pointer (CPP_264)
slides.prompt: Fill in the method used to manually release owned memory and clear a smart pointer to nullptr.
slides.codeSnippet: uniquePtr.___(); // Destroys object and sets pointer to nullptr

slides.title: std::make_shared Advantage (CPP_259)
slides.prompt: What performance advantage does std::make_shared offer over directly using 'std::shared_ptr<T>(new T())'?
options: Combines object creation and control block into a single contiguous memory allocation
Prevents derived classes from overriding base methods
Allows standard copying without updating reference counts
Bypasses thread-safety locks for faster speed
slides.correctAnswer: Combines object creation and control block into a single contiguous memory allocation
